title: The chemistry of life
note: Atoms bond according to their outer (valence) electrons. Water is polar, so its molecules hydrogen-bond to one another, which explains cohesion, high specific heat, and floating ice. Carbon forms four covalent bonds, so it can build the long, branched skeletons of organic molecules.

read.title: Water, the molecule that makes life possible
text: A water molecule is small, but its shape and charge make it unusual. Oxygen is more electronegative than hydrogen, so it pulls the shared electrons toward itself. The oxygen end carries a partial negative charge and the hydrogen ends carry partial positive charges. Water is therefore polar.

Because of this polarity, the hydrogen of one water molecule is attracted to the oxygen of a neighbor. Each attraction, a hydrogen bond, is weak and short-lived, but liquid water contains enormous numbers of them. Together they explain water's key properties. Cohesion lets water form surface tension and pull up through plant tissues. A high specific heat means a lake or a body warms and cools slowly. A high heat of vaporization means evaporating sweat carries away a lot of heat.

Hydrogen bonds also explain why ice floats. As water freezes, the bonds lock each molecule into an open lattice that is less dense than the liquid. A layer of ice insulates the water beneath it, so ponds rarely freeze solid.
Finally, polarity makes water an excellent solvent. Ions and other polar molecules dissolve readily, while nonpolar substances such as oils stay separate.
